facts.statement: Although called a quintet, only four of the galaxies are truly close together; the fifth and leftmost galaxy, NGC 7320, is well in the foreground compared with the other four.

source.title: NASA's Webb Sheds Light on Galaxy Evolution, Black Holes

facts.statement: NGC 7320 resides 40 million light-years from Earth, while the other four galaxies are about 290 million light-years away.

source.title: NASA's Webb Sheds Light on Galaxy Evolution, Black Holes

facts.statement: Webb's mosaic of Stephan's Quintet (released 12 July 2022) covers about one-fifth of the Moon's diameter, contains over 150 million pixels and is constructed from almost 1,000 separate image files.

source.title: NASA's Webb Sheds Light on Galaxy Evolution, Black Holes

facts.statement: Webb observed Stephan's Quintet in infrared light with its NIRCam and MIRI instruments; the released colours represent infrared wavelengths.
In NGC 7320, the leftmost and closest galaxy in the grouping, Webb was able to resolve individual stars and the galaxy's bright core.

source.title: NASA's Webb Sheds Light on Galaxy Evolution, Black Holes

facts.statement: The foreground galaxy is 290 - 40 = about 250 million light-years closer to us than the other four, and about seven times closer (290/40 = 7.25).
